title: I’m a graphic designer who couldn't code. AI turned me into a Project Manager of my own ideas (Built a Python RPG in 6 months).
author: AbremAv
selftext:
I’m a graphic designer, but with the rise of AI tools, I developed a massive interest in development. Programming never clicked for me before, but now everything has changed.

​The first thing I tackled was creating an RPG in Python. I decided to split the architecture right away: I built a map editor and the game itself as separate apps that share assets. The editor generates the map file, and the game loads it. I started this just to do something more productive than playing games in my free time, and without realizing it, I became a project manager.

​I control the architecture, files, and logic, while AI tools act as my "developers." I set the step-by-step roadmap, direct the workflow, review their code, and close milestones one by one. It feels like a dream come true—I can finally take the ideas out of my head and make them real. It's addictive.

​I worked on this game for six months straight. Even though it didn’t look perfect, and I later realized Python isn't the best choice for game dev, it gave me something invaluable. It introduced me to programming, the software ecosystem, and unlocked a superpower: turning ideas into working apps right here, right now.

replies.body: It's just a work in progress, but thanks for the huge compliment!

comments.author: CircularSeasoning
comments.body: "But your code has no *soul*, man. No *artistry*." Hehe.

replies.author: AbremAv
replies.body: I have to respectfully disagree! The entire process was actually under my control. The Python game was built from over 20 files, and I managed the core logic behind all of them.Also, I think you might be missing the point of the post. I don't need 'soul' in the code — I need a final product that works exactly as I envision it. Console interfaces and writing raw code just aren't my thing. I'm the person who sets the vision and brings the idea to life the way I feel it. Everyone has their own craft, and mine is definitely not coding.
